paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 19 November 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Teach one forty-minute lesson to three or four pupils. Use generic picture cards and optional safe replicas to practise careful handling and clear description. Pupils describe one feature and show the agreed care routine. No public answer or reading aloud is required.

Outcome verbatim: Handle and describe festival artefacts respectfully. Source: BUILD Weekly - Autumn!B55/C55, Autumn 2 Week 3. This row stays in Week 3. The owner moves C57 remembrance from Week 5 to Week 2 and C54 comparison from Week 2 to Week 5. Today is Thursday 19 November 2026, P3.
Theme: Identity & Belonging. Unit: Festivals & beliefs, light around the world. Term assessment: F: participation and recognition.  S: festival comparison task (Dec). This lesson is formative.

Place Support Cards page 1, Source Cards, the word mat and a visible model at each seat. Supply books and usual aids. Cut cards before the lesson. Use codes B01–B04 only. Display the starter without asking a group question.

The pack works with the supplied picture cards. Optional replicas: a plain unlit paper lantern, striped cloth and light wooden bowl. Check that items are clean, stable, smooth and suitable for this group. No flame, electrical parts, sharp edges, breakable objects, food, scent or valuable/sacred originals. Owner chooses permitted items before teaching; otherwise use cards. An adult controls access and gives object-specific instructions.

The pictures are invented teaching designs, not objects attributed to a named community. Objects can matter to people for different reasons. Describe features without judging beliefs or guessing a group from appearance. Do not use objects for costume, play fighting, ritual reenactment or jokes. No pupil must speak for a community.
Thursday 19 November 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
2 minutes settle and choice; 8 minutes picture-to-word starter with private check-ins.
5 minutes source cards with brief reset; 5 minutes model and private check; 5 minutes guided handling or observation.
10 minutes individual description and care routine with a reset; 3 minutes private feedback; 2 minutes return and exit.

“These are teaching examples. A festival is a special time people mark. An object may matter to someone. We ask before we touch. We wait for permission. We use kind words and care. You may look at a card instead. Tell or show me one thing you can see.”

Use the bowl card: “The bowl is round. I ask first and wait.” Model asking, waiting for permission, supporting a permitted item low over the table, and returning it to the mat. Never lift the lantern by its paper loop. Privately ask “Show the first step.” If ask/wait is unclear, model it again before handling. A second check is “Show the round rim.” Point to the source if needed.

A picture shows features, not actual feel or weight. Source labels give materials. Pupils may suggest “It might be used to __” but must label that as a guess. A description of a card is not evidence of handling an original object. Record picture card, replica or observation only. Observing or explaining care does not prove that the pupil handled an item.

Touch is optional. Accept HELP/PASS, pointing or a quiet request. Offer supported looking, an adult holding the card, usual aids or an agreed supervised pause. Do not ask for a reason in public. Keep participation choices separate from the outcome evidence.
Thursday 19 November 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Supported: select one feature and a care step; point, match or direct an exact scribe. Independent: write or draw one feature and a care action in a book; show the routine with the permitted item. Aspire: add a reason, a second feature or a possible use marked as a guess. Every route keeps a word bank, sentence starters and visible model. Finish: one accurate visible feature and a recorded care routine, with material and actual support stated.

Level 2 means the requested word bank, sentence starters and visible model at every task. It is not a qualification claim. Adult writes exact pupil words or selected labels, reads them back privately and invites keep/change. Record adult-supplied content. Do not infer independent reading or writing from a scribed response.

Cognition: one step and small choice set. Communication: quiet wait time, usual aid, exact scribe, plan in any language. SEMH: predictable routine and private pass. Sensory/physical: no forced touch, large cards, stable mat, adult support and usual equipment. Words, labels and position carry meaning without colour.

Use HUM-BUILD-A2-W03-E1. Record observed handling separately from stated care knowledge, plus the visible feature and actual prompts. Give one adult reply and NS, then retain the pupil’s own response. R follows actual reply, NS and own response; E follows actual banking. Leave attendance, outcomes and banking blank until they occur.
A collections helper follows handling instructions and describes objects carefully. Offer authentic pupil words or choices to the Communication portfolio. [AWARD] / [QUAL] checks stay separate.

resources.title: Staff guidance and checks
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 19 November 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Handle and describe festival artefacts respectfully. From BUILD Weekly - Autumn!B55/C55. Taught Thursday 19 November 2026, P3. Week 3 stays in place while C57 moves to Week 2 and C54 moves to Week 5 under the owner’s order. Theme: Identity & Belonging. This lesson is formative.

A is a paper lantern: folds and a loop are visible. B is cloth: stripes are visible. C is a wooden bowl: a round rim is visible. Material labels are supplied context. Accept another accurate feature supported by the picture. A screen or print image cannot establish the actual weight, feel, age or use of an original object.

Ask first; wait for permission; follow the adult’s object-specific guidance; support the permitted item low over a table; return it to the mat. Do not lift by the paper loop. A physical picture card can be handled respectfully, but record that it was a card. If the pupil only observes or states a rule, record that separately from demonstrated handling.

Display, table covering and holding things are lesson suggestions, not facts about a community. “It might be used to __” makes the inference clear. Do not assess recall of a named festival, belief or place. A replica is a copy and cannot prove how an original is used.

If a pupil reaches first, pause and model ask/wait before handling. If they state “It feels soft” from a picture, invite “It looks soft” or a visible feature; actual touch requires permission and a real item. If they infer a group from appearance, return to the visible feature and say that more information is needed.
Thursday 19 November 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
Use B04 only if a fourth pupil attends. Leave absent pupils blank. Keep each response individual, including when pupils take turns.

Keep word bank, sentence starters and a visible model on every task. Scribe exact words or labels; read back quietly for keep/change. Record adult-supplied ideas. Prompt ladder: point, short private prompt, rephrase, choice, model the first step then return the task.

No public questioning, required reading aloud or forced touch. No tasting, smelling, flames, wearing, striking or ritual enactment. Use approved lightweight replicas or the supplied cards only. Offer observation, usual aids and a private supported pause. Do not require a personal belief or family story.

Check one accurate feature and the actual care routine separately. Do not infer handling from copying a sentence. Record material and help. Offer authentic words/choices to the Communication portfolio. R follows actual adult reply, NS and own response; E follows actual banking. [AWARD] / [QUAL] decisions remain separate.
